name: file_system
description: File system tools for AI agents: read, write, and edit files, search file contents with ripgrep (grep), and find files by glob patterns across text, documents, images, audio, and video.
title: File System
author: Enconvo

commands.name: write_file
commands.title: write file
commands.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.

path.description: The file path where content will be written

content.description: The content to write to the specified file

description.description: The concise description of this task with a maximum of 100 characters

commands.name: read_file
commands.title: read File
commands.description: Read a file from the file system. Supports text files (txt, js, ts, json, md, etc.) by reading content directly, document files (pdf, epub, docx, xlsx, pptx, etc.) by extracting readable text, images by reading image content, audio by reading audio transcript, and video by reading video's audio transcript. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file.

path.description: The file path to read from

description.description: The concise description of this task with a maximum of 100 characters

commands.name: edit_file
commands.title: edit File
commands.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact line sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

description.description: The concise description of this task with a maximum of 100 characters

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

edits.description: Array of edit operations to perform

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format without making actual changes

commands.name: grep
commands.title: Grep
commands.description:
- Fast content search tool that works with any codebase size
- Searches file contents using regular expressions
- Supports full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+", etc.)
- Filter files by pattern with the include parameter (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}")
- Returns file paths and line numbers with at least one match sorted by modification time
- Use this tool when you need to find files containing specific patterns
- If you need to identify/count the number of matches within files, use the Bash tool with `rg` (ripgrep) directly. Do NOT use `grep`.
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead

pattern.description: The regex pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: The directory to search in. Defaults to the current working directory.

include.description: File pattern to include in the search (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}")

description.description: The concise description of this task with a maximum of 100 characters

commands.name: glob
commands.title: Glob
commands.description:
- Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size
- Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts"
- Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time
- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead
- You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches as a batch that are potentially useful.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

description.description: The concise description of this task with a maximum of 100 characters
